questions.title: Who will win the main MotoGP race at the 2026 British Grand Prix?
questions.background: The main Grand Prix race is separate from the sprint race held during the same MotoGP weekend.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The official MotoGP classification for the 2026 British Grand Prix main race at Silverstone. Resolution : Resolve to the rider declared the winner of the main race scheduled for August 9, 2026. The sprint race does not count. Accepted Answer Format : The winning rider's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-08-03 British GP preview updates (FIM, MotoGP.com, Crash.net, GPblog, Silverstone.co.uk) returning from MotoGP's 3-week summer break with the closest 5-way title fight in history (24 pts separating Martin 208, Ogura 194, Marc Marquez 190, Bezzecchi 186, Di Giannantonio 184): (1) Decisive medical update — defending 2025 Silverstone winner and 4-time 2026 GP winner Marco Bezzecchi IS confirmed fit and returning at Silverstone (slated for Thursday's official Pre-Event Press Conference in London), prompting a major upgrade (0.08 -> 0.16), still tempered by being only 4 weeks post-collarbone surgery and scoreless in the last 4 GPs. (2) Ai Ogura holds slight #1 favorite at 0.21 as MotoGP's highest scorer since Jerez (157 pts; 2nd Brno, 1st Assen, 2nd Sachsenring) riding the Silverstone-suited Trackhouse Aprilia. (3) Marc Marquez rises 0.16 -> 0.19 after winning 3 of the last 4 Grands Prix (Balaton Park, Brno, Sachsenring) with Crash.net noting many view him as favorite, tempered by his modest Silverstone record (no win since 2014; 11 different winners in last 11 editions). (4) Jorge Martin drops sharply 0.20 -> 0.13 as Crash.net and FIM highlight he has only 1 GP win all year (Le Mans) and just 1 podium in his last 8 races, leading on consistency rather than outright pace. (5) Fabio Di Giannantonio enters #5 at 0.08 (replacing Raul Fernandez 0.13) as 2026 Barcelona GP winner, P5 in standings, and 3rd-highest scorer since Jerez (134 pts). Note 2025 Silverstone runner-up Johann Zarco is out injured (replaced by Cal Crutchlow). Top-5 sum 0.77 leaves 23% residual for Raul Fernandez (~0.07, Assen/Sachsenring podiums on Aprilia), Pedro Acosta (~0.045), Alex Marquez (~0.04, 2025 Silverstone Sprint winner), Francesco Bagnaia (~0.035), and Silverstone parity/weather wildcards (~0.04).

questions.title: Which country will become the second, after the United States, to formally recognise Israeli sovereignty over the Golan Heights by the end of 2026?
questions.background: The United States formally recognised Israeli sovereignty over the Golan Heights in 2019. Most of the international community has rejected Israel’s annexation of the territory.

Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the first country other than the United States whose national government publicly announces formal recognition of Israeli sovereignty over the Golan Heights between January 1 and December 31, 2026. Support for Israeli security interests without explicit recognition of sovereignty does not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country’s common English name.

Introducing Colombia at #2 (0.17, replacing Papua New Guinea in top 5), trimming Argentina slightly (0.25 -> 0.23, still #1 under Milei as Israel's most aligned major ally), Paraguay (0.14 -> 0.13), Fiji (0.09 -> 0.08), and Somaliland (0.08 -> 0.07). Top-5 sum 0.68 leaves 32% residual across Papua New Guinea (~0.06), Czech Republic (~0.04, confirmed July 9-14 blocking EU settlement sanctions), Peru (~0.03, Keiko Fujimori inaugurated July 28), Ecuador (~0.03), Guatemala (~0.03), Honduras (~0.03), Micronesia/Palau/Nauru (~0.04), Kosovo (~0.02), Venezuela (~0.02, tactical rapprochement under Delcy Rodriguez), and others (~0.02).

local_articles.title: Colombia minister warns of ‘terrorism’ threat at presidential inauguration
local_articles.snippet: Colombia’s outgoing defence minister has warned of a heightened risk of “terrorism” ahead of Friday’s inauguration of President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella. Minister of Defence Pedro Sanchez told radio station La FM on Wednesday that authorities were tracking a “threat” against Friday’s proceedings. “Most likely, these criminals would attempt to disrupt this democratic event with acts of terrorism,” he said. questions.title: Who will win the Republican primary for Alabama's 2nd Congressional District on August 11, 2026?
questions.background: The primary will determine the Republican nominee for this U.S. House seat in the November 2026 general election.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Associated Press's results and reporting for Alabama's August 11, 2026 Republican primary in the 2nd Congressional District. Resolution : Resolve when AP identifies the candidate who has secured the nomination. A preliminary lead or advancement to a runoff does not count as winning the nomination. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Following the Supreme Court's June 2026 map ruling, six Republicans qualified for Alabama's August 11 special primary in AL-2, which special-session legislation made plurality-win with no runoff. State Rep. Rhett Marques already led a June 8-9 Peak Insights poll 30%-10% over Joshua McKee (with Harris and Matthews at 4%, Richardson 2%, Horn 1%, 42% undecided) before receiving endorsements from the Alabama Farmers Federation (June 18) and President Donald Trump (June 22). In a fractured six-way Alabama GOP plurality primary, Trump's endorsement plus an existing 20-point polling lead makes Marques an overwhelming favorite (~86%), with ~1% left for Christian Horn outside the top five.

questions.background: War has prevented Shakhtar Donetsk from hosting European matches in Ukraine, forcing the club to arrange alternative venues abroad.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official Shakhtar Donetsk announcement, or reliable reporting quoting the club, identifying its agreed home venue for the 2026–27 Champions League main phase. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the stadium named in the first such agreement announced by August 31, 2026. The announcement determines the answer; subsequent regulatory approval or the actual staging of matches is not required. Accepted Answer Format : The stadium’s name.
questions.current_reasoning: Complete venue overhaul driven by June 24 - July 26 reporting (BBC Sport, City AM, The Athletic via talkSPORT, Evening Standard, and UNN/Suspilne Sport): Shakhtar officially stated they are negotiating with venues in the UK and Germany (dropping Poland after Wisla Krakow's refusal), and on July 26 Shakhtar head coach Arda Turan explicitly announced 'It looks like we will play our European Cup matches in London... We are also waiting for everyone in London.' Three West London Premier League clubs with no 2026-27 European football have held talks: Brentford's Gtech Community Stadium (0.28 — earliest/longest-documented talks since June 24, established third-party rental model, UEFA compliant), Chelsea's Stamford Bridge (0.26 — 40k turnkey UCL venue, Chelsea seeking non-European revenue after finishing 10th), and Fulham's Craven Cottage (0.23 — renovated Riverside Stand and strong Shakhtar-Fulham relationship from the Kevin transfer). Keeping Veltins-Arena (0.06) as the top German fallback if London policing/council permits stall, and London Stadium (0.04) as an unconfirmed London UEFA Cat 4 fallback with West Ham in the Championship (sum 0.87, leaving 13% for other German/London venues).

questions.title: Which European country will announce a complete drought-related shutdown of its nuclear power generation between August 1 and August 13, 2026?
questions.background: Nuclear reactors require reliable cooling-water supplies. Low river levels can force reactors to shut down, potentially disrupting national electricity supplies.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official announcements by national nuclear operators or governments, corroborated by reliable news reporting. Resolution Conditions : Identify the European country that announces, between August 1 and August 13, 2026, a shutdown covering its entire operating nuclear fleet because drought has left insufficient river water for cooling. An announcement initiating the shutdown of the last operating reactor qualifies; a partial shutdown alone does not. Accepted Answer Format : The country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-08-05 update (Bloomberg/Insurance Journal Aug 5, CBS News Aug 5, Reuters/Straits Times Aug 5): Both Paks (Hungary) and Cernavoda (Romania) remain operating on one last unit as of Wednesday Aug 5 (an AFP/NDTV summary conflated earlier July 29/Aug 2 warnings as completed shutdowns, contradicted by on-the-ground Aug 5 Bloomberg and CBS reporting), but the relative margin shifted further toward Romania shutting down first. In Hungary, after Paks' overnight chief engineer came within 1 mm of switching off the last turbine, the Danube rose by a 'significant 5 centimeters' (up from +1.5 cm on Aug 4 — 'a huge stroke of luck' per Paks MP Tamas Cseh), one reactor stays at ~50% power, and PM Peter Magyar cited 'light at the end of the tunnel' with a Friday Aug 7 cold front — though Wed-Thu 40-42C heat and a 10-day dry forecast keep Paks vulnerable (trimming Hungary 0.46 -> 0.40). In Romania, Monday's 400-lb rock blast only added a few centimeters and crews are still sinking rock-filled barges on Wednesday Aug 5 trying to gain 10 cm; Deputy Energy Minister Cristian Busoi confirmed Cernavoda's second reactor must shut down without it, Defense Minister Miruta warned shutdown could come by Thursday Aug 6 if diversion fails, and Nuclearelectrica previously estimated only ~7 days of runway (~Aug 10-11) 1,200 km downstream with no relief in sight (lifting Romania 0.47 -> 0.54). Small tails on Bulgaria (0.035), Slovenia (0.01), and Switzerland (0.005) (sum 0.99).
